home.title: Cozy Safe: an open-source encrypted vault
home.desc: Cozy Safe keeps your notes, photos, videos, voice memos and files encrypted on your own device. No account, no server. Free and open source.
home.h1: A secure vault for your important data.
home.lead: Notes, photos, documents and files, encrypted right on your device. Without your password nobody can open them, not even us.
home.note: Preview. The app is new: use Back up to a file often, and don't keep the only copy of anything important here.
home.h_how: How Cozy Safe keeps you safe
home.p_how: Your data never leaves your device unencrypted, and the code that does it is public.
home.c1p: Everything is encrypted before it is written to your device. Backups and synced data are only ever encrypted data.
home.c2p: Your vault password goes with a random 24-word Recovery Key. Someone who gets hold of your files still cannot guess the password.
home.c3p: Anyone can read and check the code (GPL-3.0). Installers are built by GitHub, with provenance you can verify.
l1: Lose both the Recovery Key and the vault password, and nobody can get your data back.
Pick a password you can remember, like a short sentence.
l2: The app is new: back up to a file often.
It cannot protect a device that already has malware.
Anyone who knows the password can open the vault.
home.mac: Signed and notarized by Apple. Open the disk image and drag Cozy Safe into Applications.
home.win: Not signed yet: if SmartScreen warns you, choose More info, then Run anyway.
home.lin: Extract and run ./cozysafe. Needs GTK 3 and libsecret.
home.andr: Signed with the Cozy Pi key. When Android asks, allow your browser to install apps.
home.ios: Being tested on TestFlight, invite only for now.
home.verify: To check a download, compare it with SHA256SUMS.txt or run gh attestation verify <file> -R cozy-pi/cozysafe. Older versions are on the releases page.
home.p_see: Notes, photos, videos, voice memos and any file. These are the app's real screens, with sample content.
home.s_lock: Opens with Face ID, a fingerprint or a PIN. The lock screen shows nothing of what is inside.
home.s_library: Photos and videos. Shoot them with the app's own camera: they never reach your photo library.
home.s_notes: Notes. Lists and search show titles only, so nobody nearby can read them.
home.s_voice: Voice memos, encrypted the moment you stop recording.
home.s_group: Groups. The passport photo, its scan and the note together, open from any section.
home.s_settings: Every security setting asks for Face ID first. See at a glance what takes space.
home.c4h: None of our servers in between
home.c4p: Sync straight to your other device on the same Wi‑Fi, or through your own Google Drive. No account, no ads, no tracking.
home.c5p: Passwords and the Recovery Key stay hidden until you tap Show. Copied text is wiped after 60 seconds. Leave the app and the vault locks.
home.c6p: Back up to one encrypted file and keep it wherever you like. On a new device, open it with your Recovery Key and password.

privacy.title: Privacy policy · Cozy Safe
body: In short
Cozy Safe does not collect, send or sell any of your data. There is no account, no analytics, no advertising and no tracking in the app.
Everything you put in a vault is encrypted on your device. We cannot read it and we have no copy of it.
What stays on your device
Your vaults, notes, files and photos, always encrypted with keys derived from your vault password and Recovery Key.
App settings such as language and light or dark mode.
Where your data can go, only if you choose
A backup is one encrypted file, saved where you choose (for example iCloud Drive, Google Drive or Dropbox). Only encrypted data is written there; the provider you choose cannot read it.
Sync with your other device: when you start it and allow it, the vault's encrypted data goes over your Wi-Fi straight to your own device. Nothing goes through us or any server.

Sync through Google Drive: only if you connect your Google account. The app then keeps the vault's encrypted data in a “Cozy Safe” folder in your own Drive and can only see the files it made there. If you allow automatic sync (you can turn it off, or limit it to Wi-Fi), it updates that folder while the vault is open. Google sees encrypted files with their sizes and times, never your items' names or contents; nothing goes through us.
When you share, export or open an item in another app, that app receives an unencrypted copy and handles it under its own terms.
Permissions
Camera: only to take photos straight into a vault, when you open the camera. Photos are not saved to your photo library.
Biometrics: only if you turn on Face ID, Touch ID or fingerprint unlock. Your biometric data never leaves the device's secure hardware and is never available to the app.
Local network (iPhone) / internet (Android) / network (macOS): only for syncing with your other device on the same Wi-Fi, when you start it.
Notifications (Android): only while a sync runs, to show its progress and keep it going with the phone locked. If you say no, the sync still runs.
Internet (Google Drive): only if you connect Google Drive, to sign in with Google and reach your Drive.
This website

safe.cozypi.com is a set of static pages served by Cloudflare. It sets no cookies and runs no analytics. Cloudflare may keep standard technical logs (such as IP address) for security, under its own privacy policy. Downloads are served by GitHub.
Children
Cozy Safe is not directed at children under 13 and collects no data from anyone.
Changes and contact
If this policy changes, the new version will be published on this page with a new date.
Questions: support@cozypi.com. Cozy Safe is made by Cozy Pi, an independent studio, and its source code is public at github.com/cozy-pi/cozysafe.

feedback.title: Feedback · Cozy Safe
feedback.intro: An idea, a bug, something hard to use: tell us. We read every message.
feedback.gh_p: If you have a GitHub account, you can report a bug in public.
tips: Your app version (the Version row in Settings) and your device.
What you did, and what happened.
If the app showed an error: Settings → Report a problem → Copy details, then paste it into the email. It holds error codes only, nothing from your vault.
shot_steps: In Settings, turn off “Block screenshots” (it asks for Face ID, fingerprint or the phone's passcode).
Check it and crop out anything private.
feedback.shot_after: Turn it back on when you are done, and check the screenshot shows nothing private.
feedback.never: Never send your vault password, your Recovery Key or anything from your vault. We will never ask for them.
